title: How One Unupdated Server Cost $460 Million in 45 Minutes
alt_title_1: Inside the SEC Order on Knight Capital's 45-Minute Collapse
alt_title_2: 97 Ignored Warning Emails: The $460M Trading Bug
description_hook: According to SEC Release No. 34-70694, Knight Capital deployed new trading code manually to only seven of eight servers on August 1, 2012. In 45 minutes, dead 2003 code executed over 4 million trades and lost more than $460 million.

affiliate_cta.offer_name: Free 5-Hour Asset Builder OS + reading list
affiliate_cta.pinned_comment: 97 warning emails sat unread before the market even opened. Link to the full SEC Order PDF is in the description.

scenes.headline: $460 Million Gone in 45 Minutes
scenes.narration: One missed server update cost a Wall Street trading giant over 460 million dollars in 45 minutes.
scenes.source: SEC Release No. 34-70694, In the Matter of Knight Capital (Oct 16, 2013)

scenes.headline: Updated 7 of 8 Servers
scenes.narration: A technician manually copied new code to seven servers, missed the eighth, and accidentally woke up dead 2003 code called Power Peg.

scenes.headline: 4 Million Trades in 154 Stocks
scenes.narration: At market open, that server fired millions of orders, racking up 4 million executions across 397 million shares before engineers pulled the plug.

scenes.headline: 97 Unread Alerts & $12M Fine
scenes.narration: An internal system had sent 97 Power Peg emails before the open, but nobody treated them as alerts. Knight later paid a 12 million dollar SEC fine.
scenes.source: SEC Order para. 19, p. 6 & Section IV.C, p. 18

scenes.headline: Delete Dead Code. Build Kill Switches.
scenes.left_body: Dead code left live + no hard stop
scenes.narration: Any automated machine moving real money needs two guardrails: zero manual server deploys, and an automatic kill switch.

sources.label: SEC Administrative Order: Knight Capital Americas LLC, Rel. No. 34-70694 (Oct 16, 2013)
